methods.correlation: Normalized linear FFT cross-correlation; each phrase searched within expected musical offset±500ms, without fixing the lag. Local slices use±250ms searches and are capped at900ms to reduce beat-period ambiguity. Reported offsets are measured maxima, not assumed grid shifts.
methods.selection: Positive correlation peak; exact sample offset agreement across mix, vocals and local windows supports repeated/sample-derived components. Scores are not calibrated probability of phonetic accuracy.

keyFindings: L15/L26, L16/L27, L17/L28, L18/L29 and L19/L30 all maximize at exactly57.6s in mix, isolated vocals and filtered vocals.

Several independently aligned word windows on these shared components differ by100–304ms. These are relative inconsistencies worth reviewing, even if both model candidates individually appear plausible.
Supernova following pronouns mostly agree within80ms; the first word onset differs101ms, but its absolute beginning still needs a trusted anchor.
Now the void, every day and darkness lines do not show a strong coherent waveform match. Their musical similarity does not justify copied word timing.
Acoustic-release/reverb differences can remain even on a shared component; correlation does not automatically establish the end of the sung core.

A shared component or accompaniment leak can correlate at an exact lag while a foreground voice attacks differently. Do not infer identical foreground phonetic events from0.4–0.6 correlation alone.
decision: No timing changes recommended solely from this audit. None of the >80ms candidate onset discrepancies has local vocal correlation above0.7; moderate exact-lag agreement may partly reflect shared accompaniment leakage or a layered component. The need onset has useful corroborating cross-model boundary agreement, but target phonetic confidence is uneven and requires direct foreground inspection.
